verses.saheeh: A supplicant asked for a punishment bound to happen
verses.khattab: A challenger has demanded a punishment bound to come
verses.jalalayn: ﻿A petitioner petitioned, a supplicator supplicated [for], an impending chastisement
verses.romanUrdu: Mangne waley ne azaab maanga hai (woh azaab) jo zaroor waqey honay wala hai

verses.saheeh: To the disbelievers; of it there is no preventer.
verses.khattab: for the disbelievers—to be averted by none—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿— which in the case of the disbelievers none can avert: this was al-Nadr b. al-Hārith who said, ‘O God, if this be indeed the truth from You … [then rain down upon us stones from the heaven’ [Q. 8:32],
verses.romanUrdu: Kafiron ke liye hai, koi usey dafa karne wala nahin

verses.saheeh: [It is] from Allah, owner of the ways of ascent.
verses.khattab: from Allah, Lord of pathways of ˹heavenly˺ ascent
verses.jalalayn: ﻿from God (mina’Llāhi is semantically connected to wāqi‘in, ‘impending’), Lord of the Ascensions, the ascension routes of the angels, which are the heavens.
verses.romanUrdu: Us khuda ki taraf se hai jo urooj ke zeeno (ascending steps)ka malik hai

verses.uthmani: تَعْرُجُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ إِلَيْهِ فِى يَوْمٍۢ كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُۥ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍۢ
verses.indopak: تَعۡرُجُ الۡمَلٰٓٮِٕكَةُ وَ الرُّوۡحُ اِلَيۡهِ فِىۡ يَوۡمٍ كَانَ مِقۡدَارُهٗ خَمۡسِيۡنَ اَلۡفَ سَنَةٍ ۚ
verses.transliteration: ta'ruju almalaikatu waalrroohu ilayhi fee yawmin kana miqdaruhu khamseena alfa sanatin
verses.saheeh: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years.
verses.khattab: ˹through which˺ the angels and the ˹holy˺ spirit will ascend to Him on a Day fifty thousand years in length
verses.jalalayn: ﻿To Him, to the place in the heaven to which His command descends, ascend (read [feminine person] ta‘ruju or [masculine person] ya‘ruju) the angels and the Spirit, Gabriel, in a day (fī yawmin is semantically connected to an omitted clause, that is to say, ‘[in a day] in which the chastisement befalls them’, on the Day of Resurrection) whose span is fifty thousand years, from the perspective of the disbeliever, on account of the calamities he will encounter in it — but as for the believer, it [the mentioned day] will be easier for him than an obligatory prayer which he performs in this world, as stated in hadīth.
verses.romanUrdu: Malaika (angels) aur rooh(Jibrael) uske huzoor chadh kar jatey hain ek aise din mein jiski miqdar pacchas (fifty) hazar saal hai

verses.saheeh: So be patient with gracious patience.
verses.khattab: So endure ˹this denial, O Prophet,˺ with beautiful patience
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So be patient — this was [revealed] before he [the Prophet] was commanded to fight — with a graceful patience, that is, one in which there is no anguish.
verses.romanUrdu: Pas aey Nabi, sabr karo, shaista sabr

verses.saheeh: Indeed, they see it [as] distant,
verses.khattab: They truly see this ˹Day˺ as impossible
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Lo! they see it, that is, the chastisement, as [being] far off, as never taking place;
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh log usey dur samajhte hain

verses.saheeh: But We see it [as] near.
verses.khattab: but We see it as inevitable
verses.jalalayn: ﻿while We see it [to be] near, taking place without a doubt.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur hum usey qareeb dekh rahey hain

verses.saheeh: On the Day the sky will be like murky oil,
verses.khattab: On that Day the sky will be like molten brass
verses.jalalayn: ﻿The day when the heaven will be (yawma takūnu’l-samā’u is semantically connected to an omitted clause, implicitly taken to be yaqa‘u, ‘it will take place’) as molten silver,
verses.romanUrdu: (woh azaab us roz hoga) jis roz aasman pigli huye chandi ki tarah ho jayega

verses.saheeh: And the mountains will be like wool,
verses.khattab: and the mountains like ˹tufts of˺ wool
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and the mountains will be as flakes of wool, in terms of [their] lightness and [their] floating about in the wind.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur pahad rang-bi-rang ke dhunke huey oon (wool) jaise ho jayenge

verses.saheeh: And no friend will ask [anything of] a friend,
verses.khattab: And no close friend will ask ˹about˺ their friends
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And no friend will inquire about his friend, [no] relative [will inquire] about his relative, each being preoccupied with his own predicament.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur koi jigri dost apne jigri dost ko na puchega

verses.uthmani: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمْ ۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلْمُجْرِمُ لَوْ يَفْتَدِى مِنْ عَذَابِ يَوْمِئِذٍۭ بِبَنِيهِ
verses.indopak: يُّبَصَّرُوۡنَهُمۡ ؕ يَوَدُّ الۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِىۡ مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِٮِٕذٍۢ بِبَنِيۡهِ ۙ
verses.transliteration: yubassaroonahum yawaddu almujrimu law yaftadee min 'athabi yawmiithin bibaneehi
verses.saheeh: They will be shown each other. The criminal will wish that he could be ransomed from the punishment of that Day by his children
verses.khattab: ˹although˺ they will be made to see each other. The wicked will wish to ransom themselves from the punishment of that Day by their children
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They will [however] be made to see them, that is, friends will catch sight of one another, recognising one another but refraining from speaking [to one another] (the sentence [yubassarūnahum] is a new [independent] one). The guilty one will desire, the disbeliever will yearn, to ransom himself from the chastisement of that day (read [min ‘adhābi] yawmi’dhin or [min ‘adhābin] yawma’idhin) at the price of his children,
verses.romanUrdu: Halaanke woh ek dusre ko dikhaye jayenge, mujrim chahega ke us din ke azaab se bachne ke liye apni aulad ko

wbw.translation: They will be made to see each other

verses.saheeh: And his wife and his brother
verses.khattab: their spouses, their siblings
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and his companion, his wife, and his brother,
verses.romanUrdu: Apni biwi ko, apne bhai ko

verses.saheeh: And his nearest kindred who shelter him
verses.khattab: their clan that sheltered them
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and his kin, his clan ([expressed as fasīla] because he is a [detached] part [fasl] of it) that had sheltered him, embraced him,
verses.romanUrdu: Apne qareeb-tareen khandaan ko jo usey panaah dene wala tha

verses.uthmani: وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
verses.indopak: وَمَنۡ فِى الۡاَرۡضِ جَمِيۡعًا ۙ ثُمَّ يُنۡجِيۡهِ ۙ
verses.transliteration: waman fee alardi jamee'an thumma yunjeehi
verses.saheeh: And whoever is on earth entirely [so] then it could save him.
verses.khattab: and everyone on earth altogether, just to save themselves
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and all who are on earth, if it, that ransom, might then deliver him (thumma yunjīhi is a supplement to yaftadī, ‘to ransom himself’).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur rooh-e-zameen ke sab logon ko fidiya (badle) mein dey-de aur yeh tadbeer usey nijaat dila de

verses.saheeh: No! Indeed, it is the Flame [of Hell],
verses.khattab: But no! There will certainly be a raging Flame
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay! — a refutation of his wish. Lo! [for him] it, namely, the Fire, will be the Churning Fire (lazā) — a name for Hell, [so called] because it churns its flames [tatalazzā] against the disbelievers,
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin woh to bhadakti hui aag ki lapat hogi

verses.saheeh: A remover of exteriors.
verses.khattab: ripping off scalps
verses.jalalayn: ﻿ripping out the scalp (shawā is the plural of shawāt, the skin of the head);
verses.romanUrdu: Jo gosht posht ko chaat jayegi

wbw.translation: of the skin of the head

verses.saheeh: It invites he who turned his back [on truth] and went away [from obedience]
verses.khattab: It will summon whoever turned their backs ˹on Allah˺ and turned away ˹from the truth˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿it will call him who turned his back and ignored, faith, saying [to him]: ‘To me! to me [come hither]!’,
verses.romanUrdu: Pukar pukar kar apni taraf bulayegi har us shaks ko jisne haqq se mooh moda aur peet pheri

verses.saheeh: And collected [wealth] and hoarded.
verses.khattab: and gathered and hoarded ˹wealth˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and amassed, wealth, then hoarded, keeping it in containers and refraining from paying from it what is God’s due.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur maal jamaa kiya aur seint seint kar (amassed wealth) rakkha

verses.saheeh: Indeed, mankind was created anxious:
verses.khattab: Indeed, humankind was created impatient
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Indeed man was created restless: (halū‘an is an implied circumstantial qualifier, the explanation of which [follows]):
verses.romanUrdu: Insan thud-dila (impatient) paida kiya gaya hai

verses.saheeh: When evil touches him, impatient,
verses.khattab: distressed when touched with evil
verses.jalalayn: ﻿when evil befalls him, [he is] anxious, at the point of that evil befalling [him],
verses.romanUrdu: Jab uspar museebat aati hai to ghabra uthta hai

verses.saheeh: And when good touches him, withholding [of it],
verses.khattab: and withholding when touched with good—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and when good befalls him, [he is] grudging, at the point of that good befalling [him], that is to say, [when] wealth [befalls him], [he is grudging to give] of it what is due to God;
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jab usey khush-haali naseeb hoti hai to bukhl (kanjoosi) karne lagta hai

verses.saheeh: Except the observers of prayer -
verses.khattab: except those who pray
verses.jalalayn: ﻿except those who perform prayers, that is, the believers,
verses.romanUrdu: Magar woh log (is aib se bache huey hai) jo namaz padne waley hain

verses.saheeh: Those who are constant in their prayer
verses.khattab: consistently performing their prayers
verses.jalalayn: ﻿those who maintain, [those who] regularly observe, their prayers,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo apni namaz ki hamesha pabandi karte hai

verses.saheeh: And those within whose wealth is a known right
verses.khattab: and who give the rightful share of their wealth
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and in whose wealth there is an acknowledged due, namely, alms,
verses.romanUrdu: Jinke maalon mein

verses.saheeh: For the petitioner and the deprived -
verses.khattab: to the beggar and the poor
verses.jalalayn: ﻿for the beggar and the deprived, the [latter being the] one who refrains from begging and thus becomes deprived,
verses.romanUrdu: Saahil (maangne waley) aur mehroom ka ek haqq mukarrar hai

verses.saheeh: And those who believe in the Day of Recompense
verses.khattab: and who ˹firmly˺ believe in the Day of Judgment
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and who affirm the truth of the Day of Judgement, [of] Requital,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo roz-e-jaza ko barhaq maante hain

verses.uthmani: وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم مِّنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِم مُّشْفِقُونَ
verses.indopak: وَالَّذِيۡنَ هُمۡ مِّنۡ عَذَابِ رَبِّهِمۡ مُّشۡفِقُوۡنَ ۚ
verses.saheeh: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord -
verses.khattab: and those who fear the punishment of their Lord—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and who are apprehensive of the chastisement of their Lord —
verses.romanUrdu: Jo apne Rubb ke azaab se darte hain

verses.saheeh: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not that from which one is safe -
verses.khattab: ˹knowing that˺ none should feel secure from their Lord’s punishment—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿lo! there is no security from the chastisement of their Lord, [from] its being sent down —
verses.romanUrdu: Kyunke unke Rubb ka azaab aisi cheez nahin hai jissey koi bekhauf ho

verses.saheeh: And those who guard their private parts
verses.khattab: and those who guard their chastity
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and those who guard their private parts,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo apni sharmgahon ki hifazat karte hain

verses.uthmani: إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ غَيْرُ مَلُومِينَ
verses.indopak: اِلَّا عَلٰٓى اَزۡوَاجِهِمۡ اَوۡ مَا مَلَـكَتۡ اَيۡمَانُهُمۡ فَاِنَّهُمۡ غَيۡرُ مَلُوۡمِيۡنَ ۚ
verses.transliteration: illa 'ala azwajihim aw ma malakat aymanuhum fainnahum ghayru maloomeena
verses.saheeh: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed -
verses.khattab: except with their wives or those ˹bondwomen˺ in their possession, for then they are free from blame
verses.jalalayn: ﻿except from their wives and those whom their right hands own, in the way of slavegirls, for in that case they are not blameworthy;
verses.romanUrdu: Ba-juz apne biwiyon ya apni mamluka aurton ke jinse mehfooz na rakhne mein unpar koi malamat nahin

verses.uthmani: فَمَنِ ٱبْتَغَىٰ وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْعَادُونَ
verses.indopak: فَمَنِ ابۡتَغٰى وَرَآءَ ذٰلِكَ فَاُولٰٓٮِٕكَ هُمُ الۡعٰدُوۡنَ ۚ
verses.transliteration: famani ibtagha waraa thalika faolaika humu al'adoona
verses.saheeh: But whoever seeks beyond that, then they are the transgressors -
verses.khattab: but whoever seeks beyond that are the transgressors
verses.jalalayn: ﻿but whoever seeks beyond that, those are the infringers, who transgress [the bounds of] what is lawful [stepping] into what is unlawful;
verses.romanUrdu: Albatta jo iske alawa kuch aur chahein wahi hadd se tajawuz karne wala hai

verses.saheeh: And those who are to their trusts and promises attentive
verses.khattab: ˹The faithful are˺ also those who are true to their trusts and covenants
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and those who are keepers, [faithful] guardians, of their trusts (amānātihim: a variant reading has the singular [amānatihim]), that to which they are entrusted of religion and the affairs of this world, and their covenant, the one taken from them regarding such things,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo apne amanaton ki hifazat aur apne ahad (covenant) ka paas karte hai

verses.saheeh: And those who are in their testimonies upright
verses.khattab: and who are honest in their testimony
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and who are forthwith with their testimony (bi-shahādatihim: a variant reading has the plural [bi-shahādātihim, ‘their testimonies’]), [those who] offer them and do not withhold them,
verses.romanUrdu: Jo apni gawahiyon mein raast baazi (upright) par qayam rehte hain

verses.saheeh: And those who [carefully] maintain their prayer:
verses.khattab: and who are ˹properly˺ observant of their prayers
verses.jalalayn: ﻿and who preserve their prayers, by observing them in their appointed times.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur jo apni namaz ki hifazat karte hain

verses.saheeh: They will be in gardens, honored.
verses.khattab: These will be in Gardens, held in honour
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Those will be in Gardens, honoured.
verses.romanUrdu: Yeh log izzat ke saath jannat ke baaghon mei rahenge

verses.saheeh: So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, hastening [from] before you, [O Muhammad],
verses.khattab: So what is the matter with the disbelievers that they rush ˹head-long˺ towards you ˹O Prophet˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So what is wrong with those who disbelieve that they keep staring towards you (muhti‘īna is a circumstantial qualifier),
verses.romanUrdu: Pas aey Nabi , kya baat hai ke yeh munkirin dayein(left) aur bayein(right) se

verses.saheeh: [To sit] on [your] right and [your] left in separate groups?
verses.khattab: from the right and the left, in groups ˹to mock you˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿to the right and to the left, of you, in droves? (‘izīna is also a circumstantial qualifier), in other words, in groups standing in circles, one next to the other, saying, in mockery of the believers, ‘Verily if [the likes of] these are to enter Paradise, we shall enter it before them’. God, exalted be He, says:
verses.romanUrdu: Giroh (crowds) dar giroh(crowds) tumhari taraf daude chale aa rahe hain

verses.uthmani: أَيَطْمَعُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۢ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُدْخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيمٍۢ
verses.indopak: اَيَطۡمَعُ كُلُّ امۡرِىءٍ مِّنۡهُمۡ اَنۡ يُّدۡخَلَ جَنَّةَ نَعِيۡمٍ ۙ
verses.transliteration: ayatma'u kullu imriin minhum an yudkhala jannata na'eemin
verses.saheeh: Does every person among them aspire to enter a garden of pleasure?
verses.khattab: Does every one of them expect to be admitted into a Garden of Bliss
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Does each one of them hope to be admitted into a Garden of Bliss?
verses.romanUrdu: Kya inmein se har ek yeh lalaj rakhta hai ke woh niyamat bhari jannat mein daakhil kardiya jayega

verses.saheeh: No! Indeed, We have created them from that which they know.
verses.khattab: But no! Indeed, they ˹already˺ know what We created them from
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nay! — meant to thwart their hopes of [entering] Paradise. Indeed We created them, as others, from what they know, from drops of sperm, and so one cannot hope for Paradise [merely] on account of this: one hopes for it by being God-fearing.
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz nahin humne jis cheez se inko paida kiya hai usey yeh khud jaante hain

verses.uthmani: فَلَآ أُقْسِمُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْمَشَٰرِقِ وَٱلْمَغَٰرِبِ إِنَّا لَقَٰدِرُونَ
verses.indopak: فَلَاۤ اُقۡسِمُ بِرَبِّ الۡمَشٰرِقِ وَالۡمَغٰرِبِ اِنَّا لَقٰدِرُوۡنَ ۙ
verses.transliteration: fala oqsimu birabbi almashariqi waalmagharibi inna laqadiroona
verses.saheeh: So I swear by the Lord of [all] risings and settings that indeed We are able
verses.khattab: So, I do swear by the Lord of ˹all˺ the points of sunrise and sunset that We are truly capable
verses.jalalayn: ﻿For verily (fa-lā: lā is extra) I swear by the Lord of the rising-places and the setting-places, of the sun, the moon and all the stars, that We are able
verses.romanUrdu: Pas nahin, main qasam khata hoon mashrikon aur maghribon ke maalik ki hum ispar qadir hain

verses.uthmani: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ خَيْرًۭا مِّنْهُمْ وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ
verses.indopak: عَلٰٓى اَنۡ نُّبَدِّلَ خَيۡرًا مِّنۡهُمۡ ۙ وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمَسۡبُوۡقِيۡنَ
verses.transliteration: 'ala an nubaddila khayran minhum wama nahnu bimasbooqeena
verses.saheeh: To replace them with better than them; and We are not to be outdone.
verses.khattab: of replacing them with ˹others˺ better than them, and We cannot be prevented ˹from doing so˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿to replace [them], to bring in their place, with [others] better than them, and We are not to be outmanoeuvred, [We will not be] frustrated in this.
verses.romanUrdu: Ke inki jagah insey behtar log le aayein aur koi humse baazi le jaane wala nahin hai

verses.uthmani: فَذَرْهُمْ يَخُوضُوا۟ وَيَلْعَبُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يُوعَدُونَ
verses.indopak: فَذَرۡهُمۡ يَخُوۡضُوۡا وَيَلۡعَبُوۡا حَتّٰى يُلٰقُوۡا يَوۡمَهُمُ الَّذِىۡ يُوۡعَدُوۡنَ ۙ
verses.transliteration: fatharhum yakhoodoo wayal'aboo hatta yulaqoo yawmahumu allathee yoo'adoona
verses.saheeh: So leave them to converse vainly and amuse themselves until they meet their Day which they are promised -
verses.khattab: So let them indulge ˹in falsehood˺ and amuse ˹themselves˺ until they face their Day, which they have been threatened with—
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So leave them to indulge, in their falsehoods, and to play, in this world of theirs, until they encounter that day of theirs, in, which they are promised, chastisement;
verses.romanUrdu: Lihaza inhein apni behuda baaton aur apne khel mein pada rehne do yahan tak ke yeh apne us din ko pahunch jayenge jiska insey waada kiya ja raha hai

verses.uthmani: يَوْمَ يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًۭا كَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَىٰ نُصُبٍۢ يُوفِضُونَ
verses.indopak: يَوۡمَ يَخۡرُجُوۡنَ مِنَ الۡاَجۡدَاثِ سِرَاعًا كَاَنَّهُمۡ اِلٰى نُصُبٍ يُّوۡفِضُوۡنَ ۙ
verses.transliteration: yawma yakhrujoona mina alajdathi sira'an kaannahum ila nusubin yoofidoona
verses.saheeh: The Day they will emerge from the graves rapidly as if they were, toward an erected idol, hastening.
verses.khattab: the Day they will come forth from the graves swiftly, as if racing to an idol ˹for a blessing˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿the day when they will come forth from the graves hastening, to the site of the Gathering, as if racing to a [standing] target (nasbin: a variant reading has nusubin, meaning something that has been erected [mansūb], such as a flag or a banner),
verses.romanUrdu: Jab yeh apni qabron se nikal kar is tarah daude ja rahey hongey jaise apne buthon (idols) ke aasthano (altars) ki taraf daud rahey hon

verses.uthmani: خَٰشِعَةً أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌۭ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا۟ يُوعَدُونَ
verses.indopak: خَاشِعَةً اَبۡصَارُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةٌ ؕ ذٰلِكَ الۡيَوۡمُ الَّذِىۡ كَانُوۡا يُوۡعَدُوۡنَ
verses.transliteration: khashi'atan absaruhum tarhaquhum thillatun thalika alyawmu allathee kanoo yoo'adoona
verses.saheeh: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. That is the Day which they had been promised.
verses.khattab: with eyes downcast, utterly covered with disgrace. That is the Day they have ˹always˺ been warned of
verses.jalalayn: ﻿with their eyes humbled, abject, overcast by abasement, shrouded in it. Such is the day which they are promised (dhālika is the subject and what follows it is the predicate), meaning: the Day of Resurrection.
verses.romanUrdu: Inki nigahein jhuki hui hongi, zillat inpar chaa rahi hogi, woh din hai jiska insey wada kiya ja raha hai
